system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty cap: 20% of price (A$4.8m). | Higher cap, ideally 30–50% for general warranties, with separate uncapped/super-cap categories. | **Reject 20% as sole recourse; seek 30% minimum plus category carve-outs** — known and material risks exceed a thin general cap. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | A$25k de minimis; A$250k deductible basket; recovery only above basket. | Lower de minimis and tipping basket, or at least a lower deductible basket; aggregate related claims. | **Seek A$10k de minimis and A$100k tipping basket (or deductible only if substantially reduced)** — the proposed structure excludes smaller but recurrent losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | All general claims expire 18 months after Completion; Seller seeks broad application to all claims. | At least 24 months for business warranties; longer statutory periods for tax, IP, employment and privacy/data claims. | **Reject universal 18 months; adopt category-specific survival** — several liabilities may not emerge within 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Title, capacity, authority and ownership warranties uncapped (or capped at 100% of price) and surviving for the limitation period. | **Require a separate fundamental-warranty regime: 100% cap and at least 6 years** — Buyer must receive durable recourse if it does not acquire what it paid for. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims; no express fraud carve-out identified. | Express preservation of claims for fraud, fraudulent concealment and wilful misconduct, without cap, basket or time-bar to the fullest extent permitted. | **Insert an express fraud/fraudulent-concealment carve-out** — blanket limitations must not shield dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Deems all data-room materials, accounts, registers and public records generally disclosed. | Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception; no data-room/public-record sweep-up. | **Delete general disclosure and limit disclosure to specifically indexed, fair disclosures** — volume of material is not meaningful notice of a warranty breach. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from data room/public records. | No actual/constructive knowledge bar, or only actual knowledge of named senior Buyer deal team members, evidenced in writing and expressly identified as a warranty exception. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-knowledge language; tightly limit any actual-knowledge qualifier** — it improperly shifts Seller warranty risk into Buyer DD. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller says it will use reasonable endeavours; regards written consent as satisfying the issue. Bluefen represents about A$3.6m/30% FY26 revenue, and no final consent or satisfaction of conditions is provided. | Completion conditional on unconditional written consent, all conditions satisfied/waived, and no adverse amendment or termination right. | **Make final unconditional Bluefen consent a Completion condition, with termination right or holdback if absent** — loss or disruption of a 30% revenue customer is material. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approx. A$3.2m remains outstanding; discharge/release to follow Completion. | Debt repaid at or before Completion, with contemporaneous executed releases of all security and guarantees. | **Require pay-off from Completion proceeds and simultaneous releases as a Completion deliverable** — Buyer cannot take a debt-free/cash-free target subject to live debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | A$420k conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; treatment of payroll tax, super and on-costs unstated. | Seller-funded payment or price reduction/escrow covering the full liability, including payroll tax, super, leave and other on-costs; clear post-Completion responsibility. | **Deduct/escrow the fully loaded bonus amount from consideration and obtain a specific indemnity** — it is a transaction-linked liability not reflected in price mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; A$180k remains open, and no evidence of payment or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Specific indemnity for all IP ownership/use/infringement and remediation losses; payment evidence and irrevocable assignment/confirmation before Completion. | **Expand the indemnity and make IP-chain confirmation a Completion deliverable** — SOW3 materials may be essential to the business yet ownership remains conditional. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected material; no confirmed access, scope or notification determination. | Ongoing investigation, prompt reporting, appropriate containment/remediation, a specific indemnity/escrow, and no warranty qualification merely because it was disclosed. | **Require a closing update, remediation plan and specific indemnity or escrow** — regulatory, notification and customer exposure can crystallise after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling A$330k characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Full contracts and timing/termination analysis; covenant not to renew/commit outside ordinary course; price adjustment or specific treatment if non-terminable/unbudgeted. | **Do not accept the characterisation without evidence; reserve a price adjustment or indemnity** — “ordinary course” does not establish whether Buyer is inheriting avoidable or unaccrued commitments. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller seeks limitations and time bars applying to all claims unless expressly excluded; tax/IP said to sit in the general regime. | Separate regimes for fundamental/title, tax, IP, employment, privacy/data, specified indemnities and restrictive covenant claims. | **Expressly ring-fence each special category from general caps, baskets and survival periods** — a general limitation clause must not silently dilute negotiated specialist protection. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller owns 100%; disclosure says Buyer must do its own verification. | Positive title warranty; Completion deliverables including original/valid share transfers, board approvals, updated register, certificates (if any), no encumbrance releases and ASIC/register evidence. | **Require documentary title and no-encumbrance verification at Completion, backed by the fundamental regime** — a register extract alone does not establish transferable, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller treats tax and IP warranties as settled under the general 20%/18-month regime. | Dedicated tax covenant/indemnity (typically post-completion statutory limitation period, no basket and separate cap) and robust IP warranties/indemnity with longer survival. | **Reopen and document standalone tax and IP protection** — tax exposures and IP defects often surface later and can exceed the general warranty package. |
=== END ADVICE ===
